The surface of a silicon crystal imaged using a scanning tunneling microscope. Individual silicon atoms appear as purple protrusions above the background. The surface was cleaned in an ultrahigh vacuum to remove all impurity atoms and the image was taken at very low temperatures (2220°C) to obtain the high resolution shown here. There are two kinds of surface silicon atoms shown in this image: “corner” silicon atoms that form hexagonal rings around a hole in the surface layer and “center” silicon atoms that appear as pairs arranged around the hexagonal rings.
